user_query: I want to cancel my beauty package but they refuse to refund.
variations: Cancel gym membership, they demand penalty
part_a_general_info: Under the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act (CPFTA), it is an unfair practice to exert undue pressure or influence on a consumer. Cooling-off period: Certain contracts (e.g., timeshares, direct sales) have a mandatory cooling-off period (usually 5 days). General beauty and gym packages do not automatically have a cooling-off period unless the contract states so or the business is accredited with CaseTrust. CaseTrust-accredited businesses are required to provide a cooling-off period, typically 5 working days from the date of signing. If you were subjected to high-pressure sales tactics (e.g., not allowed to leave the premises), this may constitute an unfair practice under the CPFTA.
triage_questions: Q1: When did you sign the contract?
Q2: Were you forced or pressured into signing (e.g., not allowed to leave)?
Q3: Does the business have CaseTrust accreditation?
Q4: What does the contract say about cancellation?
branching_logic: If Q3 = CaseTrust accredited → Usually has a 5-day cooling-off period. Check if still within window.
If Q2 = Yes (pressure/duress) → Possible CPFTA unfair practice claim.
routing: Route A (Dispute, CASE mediation): Lodge complaint with CASE (Consumers Association of Singapore). CASE will mediate.
Route B (CASE mediation fails): File claim at Small Claims Tribunal (SCT) if within jurisdiction.
guardrail: Must NOT interpret the specific contract clauses for the user.
